taxonomy.safe-centre-claim: A defector claims a role it knows (census) or guesses lies in the centre, so nobody can counter-claim it.
taxonomy.counter-claim-info-role: A defector claims the same information role as an honest player (a Sage duel, a Herder duel...).
taxonomy.fake-read: A false report of a night look at a player (true role claimed or not).
taxonomy.frame-ally: A defector accuses or lets the table eliminate its own team-mate who is not a Werewolf (a decoy whose elimination wins).
taxonomy.false-movement-story: A false account of night card movement (a rotation's direction or targets, a swap that did not happen).
taxonomy.fake-confession: A player falsely admits to a role or a team to steer the vote.
taxonomy.vote-split-or-tie-plan: Someone proposes splitting votes or engineering a tie.
taxonomy.phoenix-baiting: A Pyre player acts or is presented as a wolf to draw the votes onto a Phoenix/Kindler.
taxonomy.census-backward-induction: Someone argues from what a wolf's census would have told it ("a wolf would never claim X").
taxonomy.motive-analysis: Someone argues from who benefits / why a player would lie (incentive reasoning beyond the mechanics).
taxonomy.claim-timing-tell: Someone argues from when or how a player claimed (late, hedged, changed claim).
taxonomy.claim-count-collision: A contradiction in role counts (two players claim a single card, more claims than copies) exposed someone.
taxonomy.corroboration-chain: Two or more honest results are lined up to confirm a player or a card.
taxonomy.team-collision: Two members of the same defecting team told incompatible stories, hurting their team.
taxonomy.retarget-the-swapper: The table chooses to eliminate a player who could act after the talk, rather than the obvious suspect.

rankingRule: talk-live share of fixed scenarios, then judge ToM, then share of games with 0.6 <= c < 1, then lower noise
